title: J.C. Watts: From Sooners Quarterback to the U.S. Congress
question: Which former OU quarterback became a U.S. Congressman?
answer: J.C. Watts, OU's starting quarterback in 1979 and 1980, later represented Oklahoma in the U.S. House from 1995 to 2003 and chaired the House Republican Conference.
summary: J.C. Watts led OU to back-to-back Orange Bowl wins, played in the CFL, then served Oklahoma in Congress from 1995 to 2003 and chaired the House GOP Conference.
body: Before he was a familiar face on Capitol Hill, Julius Caesar "J.C." Watts Jr. was a quarterback from Eufaula who climbed the Oklahoma depth chart the hard way. He arrived in Norman as a seventh-string option and became the starter in 1979, and ran the Sooners' offense through the 1979 and 1980 seasons.

Those two years ended in Miami. Watts led Oklahoma to Orange Bowl victories in 1980 and 1981 and was named the game's most valuable player both times, which later earned him a spot in the Orange Bowl Hall of Fame in 1992. He finished his journalism studies at OU and took his arm north rather than switch positions in the NFL.

In the Canadian Football League, Watts played for the Ottawa Rough Riders and later the Toronto Argonauts from 1981 to 1986, and he helped Ottawa reach the Grey Cup in his rookie season. Back home, he worked as a youth minister in Del City and started a highway construction company.

His public service career began in 1990, when he won a seat on the Oklahoma Corporation Commission, where he later served as chairman. In 1994 voters sent him to the U.S. House, and he represented Oklahoma from 1995 to 2003. His colleagues elected him chairman of the House Republican Conference, a leadership post he held through his final term.

Watts chose not to seek re-election in 2002, saying he wanted more time with his family, and went on to build a consulting business and work as a political analyst. For Sooner fans, he remains one of the clearest examples of a player whose leadership carried well past the goal line.
